pages.title: MDLog and Journaler: the per-rank metadata journal

features.name: Per-rank metadata write-ahead journal (MDLog)
features.description: Every metadata mutation of a rank is journaled as a LogEvent before it is made visible as safe; one journal per rank, totally ordered by event_seq; dirty objects are written back lazily per segment and the journal is trimmed afterwards.
features.notes: Durability of metadata operations (POSIX fsync/sync semantics for metadata) rests on it.

features.name: JournalPointer object (front/back journal inode)
features.description: Object <0x400+rank>.00000000 holds {front, back} (ENCODE_START(1,1), two u64). front is the active journal inode (default 0x200+rank); back is non-zero only during a journal rewrite. Created if missing; back journal erased on startup if a rewrite was interrupted.
features.notes: Read by cephfs-journal-tool (JournalScanner::scan_pointer) and rewritten by Resetter --force.

features.name: Journaler header object
features.description: Object <ino>.00000000 written with write_full: ENCODE_START(2,2){magic 'ceph fs volume v011', trimmed_pos, expire_pos, unused_field(=expire_pos), write_pos(=safe_pos), legacy ceph_file_layout, u8 stream_format}. Validated on read (magic, write_pos>=expire_pos>=trimmed_pos).

features.name: Journal byte stream striped over RADOS objects
features.description: Journal data is a linear byte stream mapped by file_layout_t (default 4 MiB objects, stripe_count 1) to objects '%llx.%08llx' (ino, objno); data starts at offset = one period (object 1); object 0 holds only the header.
features.notes: mds_log_segment_size overrides object size for new journals only.

features.name: RESILIENT entry framing
features.description: Each entry = le64 sentinel 0x3141592653589793, le32 size, payload, le64 start_ptr (absolute offset of the entry). Bad sentinel -> -EINVAL; start_ptr mismatch asserts. Lets offline tools resynchronise in damaged journals. No checksum.

features.name: Legacy journal format and automatic reformat
features.description: Journals in an older stream format than mds_journal_format are rewritten to the alternate inode (0x300+rank / 0x200+rank) using JournalPointer back, then pointers are swapped and the old journal erased. Standby-replay tolerates old formats until takeover, then MDLog::reopen reformats.
features.notes: Only relevant for pre-RESILIENT journals (format 0).

features.name: LogEvent envelope
features.description: Payload = le32 EVENT_NEW_ENCODING(0) + ENCODE_START(1,1){le32 type, event body}; the body is encoded with MDLog::mdsmap_up_features, a single member overwritten by every _submit_entry and read when the submit thread dequeues the event (so the features of the most recent submission). decode_event also accepts the pre-versioned form and returns nullptr on unknown type or decode error, but asserts the payload was fully consumed (trailing bytes abort).

features.name: Asynchronous submit pipeline (mds-log-submit thread)
features.description: submit_entry (under mds_lock) assigns event_seq, attaches the event to the current segment, runs update_segment and queues a PendingEvent; a dedicated thread encodes events without mds_lock, appends them to the Journaler and registers completions with wait_for_flush.
features.notes: The Objecter op budget (objecter_inflight_ops/bytes) does not block in the MDS: its Objecter does not set keep_balanced_budget, so _take_op_budget uses non-blocking Throttle::take.

features.name: Group commit via explicit flush
features.description: Appended entries stay in the Journaler write buffer until MDLog::flush() (or an object boundary) triggers one RADOS write per object for everything buffered; ~62 call sites flush before waiting; Server::journal_and_reply flushes only if no early reply was sent.
features.notes: Determines latency of safe replies. Journaler::flush(ctx) completes ctx immediately when nothing is buffered even if earlier flushes are uncommitted (Journaler.cc:792); MDLog never passes a ctx, _reformat_journal and Resetter do.

features.name: Periodic flush on tick
features.description: MDSRankDispatcher::tick calls mdlog->flush() every mds_tick_interval (5 s), bounding how long an unflushed event (e.g. after an early reply) can wait; the whole tick returns early while the beacon is laggy, so no periodic flush happens then.
features.notes: kclient comment assumes 'at most 5 seconds' (linux/fs/ceph/caps.c:2430).

features.name: Client-requested journal flush (CEPH_SESSION_REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG)
features.description: MClientSession op 12; the MDS calls mdlog->flush() if up:active and sends no reply. Sent by kclient on fsync with unsafe requests, syncfs, pre-umount, reset; by libcephfs on fsync, sync_fs, unmount.
features.notes: Clients only send it when the MDS connection advertises SERVER_LUMINOUS.

features.name: wait_for_safe barrier
features.description: Fires a context once every event submitted so far is durable (queued behind pending events, or registered directly with the Journaler); does not flush by itself. Used by Migrator export, session handling, flush journal, boot.

features.name: Ordered completion and safe_pos tracking
features.description: Journaler advances safe_pos over entry boundaries as flushes commit (conservatively when several flushes overlap) and completes waiters in offset order via the single mds-rank-fin finisher; MDSLogContextBase runs finish under mds_lock then sets MDLog::safe_pos.
features.notes: Safe replies, cap flush acks and session acks are emitted from these completions.

features.name: Prezeroing ahead of the write position
features.description: Objects up to journaler_prezero_periods periods beyond write_pos are removed (whole periods) or zeroed (partial) before data is flushed there; flushes never come within one period of prezero_pos.
features.notes: Makes end-of-log probing reliable.

features.name: End-of-journal probing on recovery
features.description: After reading the header, Filer::probe stats objects period by period from header.write_pos (ENOENT = size 0, RWORDERED) until a non-full object; that end becomes write_pos.

features.name: Torn-tail handling
features.description: If the last entry is incomplete when all data up to the probed end has been read, write_pos is rewound to the entry start and the partial bytes are later zeroed by trim_tail/prezero.

features.name: Periodic header writes
features.description: Header rewritten when expire_pos advances (MDLog::write_head after trim) and on Journaler::flush once journaler_write_head_interval (15 s) elapsed since the last header write; header write_pos = safe_pos. last_wrote_head is set only by _write_head, so a freshly recovered Journaler writes its header on its first flush.

features.name: Log segments tracking dirty state
features.description: LogSegment holds intrusive lists of dirty/new dirfrags, dirty dentries/inodes, open files, dirty backtraces, dirty scatter state, truncating/purging inodes, uncommitted leader/peer/fragment ops, pending table tids and table/inotable/sessionmap versions; an object is listed only in the newest segment that dirtied it, except new_dirfrags, which keeps a never-committed dirfrag in the oldest segment that mentions it until its first commit.

features.name: Segment boundaries: major (ESubtreeMap, ELid, EResetJournal) and minor (ESegment)
features.description: SegmentBoundary events start segments; major ones are valid replay starting points (ESubtreeMap carries the auth subtree map, ELid marks a rank without subtrees, EResetJournal a reset); ESegment is a light minor boundary.

features.name: Segment rotation policy
features.description: After each submission: new ESubtreeMap when more than mds_log_minor_segments_per_major_segment minor segments started since the last major; else ESegment when the segment spans a journal object boundary or has >= mds_log_events_per_segment events.

features.name: Stray directory rotation per segment
features.description: Starting a new segment advances the active stray directory index (stray0..stray9), except while the rank is up:stopping.

features.name: Background log trimming (mds-log-trim) with throttle
features.description: Every mds_log_trim_upkeep_interval, while active or stopping, trim() starts expiring the oldest fully-safe segments while segments > mds_log_max_segments or events > mds_log_max_events, rate-limited by a decaying counter (mds_log_trim_threshold, mds_log_trim_decay_rate); writeback priority scales with backlog.

features.name: Segment expiry (writeback obligations)
features.description: try_to_expire commits dirty/new dirfrags (or stores base inodes), waits for unfreeze, uncommitted leaders/peers/fragments, nudges scatterlocks, rejournals snapped open inodes, waits for OFT commit, stores backtraces, saves inotable/sessionmap/table servers, waits for table acks, truncates and purges; retried until nothing is left.

features.name: Major-segment-granular trimming and expire_pos
features.description: Expired segments are removed only in whole groups ending right before a major segment; Journaler expire_pos is set to the start of that major boundary; the newest segment is never deleted because deletion requires a later major segment (when capped it can only be marked expired).

features.name: Journal object deletion
features.description: After a header with a newer expire_pos commits, Journaler::_trim purges whole objects below it (one purge at a time, filer_max_purge_ops removes in flight).

features.name: OpenFileTable commit gating of expiry
features.description: A segment with seq >= OpenFileTable committed_log_seq cannot expire until an OFT commit covering it completes; trim() triggers OFT commits for the newest segment seq.
features.notes: Open files are no longer rejournaled every segment; the OFT replaces that.

features.name: Rejournaling of snapshotted open inodes at expiry
features.description: Open snapshotted inodes with client_snap_caps (pending snapflush) are re-logged in an EOpen in the current segment before an old segment can expire.

features.name: EMetaBlob ancestor elision relative to last major segment
features.description: EMetaBlob::add_dir_context (TO_AUTH_SUBTREE_ROOT mode) marks the parent dentry of a directory whose inode was journaled since the last major segment (CInode::last_journaled), and all ancestors above it, as 'maybe' context and drops them only if the walk reaches an unambiguous auth subtree root; this relies on replay always starting at a major boundary.

features.name: flush journal admin command
features.description: asok/tell 'flush journal': new ESubtreeMap, flush, wait_for_safe, trim_to, wait for all expiring segments, trim and write header; replies {message, return_code}; -EROFS when read-only; no-op unless active.
features.notes: first-damage.py runbook and many qa tests call it.

features.name: cache drop includes journal flush
features.description: 'cache drop [timeout]' recalls client state then runs the flush-journal state machine and reports a flush_journal section.

features.name: Explicit trimming and log capping on stop
features.description: During up:stopping, MDCache::shutdown_pass journals a subtree map if needed, calls trim_all until one segment remains, then submits ELid, flushes and caps the log; afterwards no event may be submitted and the journal starts at that ELid.
features.notes: Needed to reach down:stopped (max_mds reduction, upgrades).

features.name: Journal creation for a new rank
features.description: up:creating: MDLog::create writes a fresh header and pointer, submits ELid as first (major) segment, builds the hierarchy, then journals an ESubtreeMap and waits for it to be safe before requesting active.

features.name: Positioning at end without replay (up:starting)
features.description: A previously stopped rank opens its journal, positions read/expire at write_pos (append) and journals a fresh ESubtreeMap without replaying.

features.name: Journal recovery thread
features.description: mds-log-recvr: blocking load/create of the pointer, cleanup of an interrupted rewrite, header read + probe of the front journal, format check, possibly reformat; respawn on blocklist, damaged on other errors.

features.name: Journal replay
features.description: mds-log-replay reads entries from expire_pos to the probed end, rebuilds segments from boundary events, and replays each event under mds_lock; replay re-dirties objects into the replayed segments.
features.notes: Crash consistency of metadata.

features.name: Replay error policy and skip options
features.description: Missing objects and corrupt framing/events mark the rank damaged; mds_log_skip_corrupt_events and mds_log_skip_unbounded_events allow skipping; an ELid in mid-journal is ignored; events before the first major boundary are unbounded.
features.notes: MDLog::replay asserts the journaler is read-only (MDLog.cc:1030), so the 'invalid journaler offsets' damaged branch of _replay_thread is unreachable; read_pos < expire_pos yields -EAGAIN, which boot_start turns into a respawn only in up:standby-replay and into suicide() in up:replay (MDSRank.cc:1626-1642).

features.name: Replay progress estimate and MDS_ESTIMATED_REPLAY_TIME
features.description: Percent complete from (read_pos - trimmed_pos)/(write_pos - trimmed_pos) and elapsed time; beacon raises MDS_ESTIMATED_REPLAY_TIME after 30 s in up:replay.

features.name: replay_status in status command
features.description: status reports journal_read_pos, journal_write_pos, journal_expire_pos, num_events, num_segments while in replay or standby-replay.

features.name: Standby-replay journal tailing
features.description: A follower replays the active's journal read-only, re-reading header and re-probing every mds_replay_interval, dropping segments the active has expired (marking their objects clean) to keep a warm cache.
features.notes: Assigned by the mon when allow_standby_replay is set. In the replay thread's -EINVAL path standby_trim_segments() runs without mds_lock (MDLog.cc:1480), racing with mds_lock holders; standby_trim_segments never prunes major_segments, so segmjr grows on a long-running follower.

features.name: Standby-replay fall-behind detection
features.description: If the active trimmed objects past the follower's read position (old read_pos < trimmed_pos), or a read hits ENOENT, or the journal is being rewritten, the follower respawns.

features.name: Standby-replay takeover final pass
features.description: When promoted to up:replay, the follower waits for an OSD map epoch >= last_failure_osd_epoch, re-reads header/probe and replays to the end, then reformats if needed and becomes writeable.

features.name: Fencing before reading the journal
features.description: replay_start waits for the OSD map that blocklists the previous rank holder (mdsmap last_failure_osd_epoch) before opening the journal, guaranteeing a single writer.

features.name: Journal write error handling
features.description: Any journal write/header/prezero/trim error other than blocklisting marks the rank damaged (clog 'Unhandled journal write error'); blocklisted or timed-out I/O respawns the daemon.
features.notes: Requires 'ceph mds repaired' to clear.

features.name: MDS_TRIM health and mon gating of fail commands
features.description: Beacon reports MDS_TRIM 'Behind on trimming (N/M)' when segments > mds_log_max_segments * mds_log_warn_factor; the mon refuses 'mds fail' and 'fs fail' without --yes-i-really-mean-it while it is present.

features.name: Slow metadata IO health includes journal completions
features.description: Every MDSLogContextBase is a tracked MDSIOContextBase from submit time; ones older than osd_op_complaint_time raise MDS_SLOW_METADATA_IO.

features.name: mds_log perf counters
features.description: evadd, ev, seg, replayed (interesting); evlrg, evexg, evexd, segexg, segexd, segmjr, jlat, evex, evtrm, segadd, segex, segtrm (useful); expos, wrpos, rdpos (debug).
features.notes: Consumed by mgr status (mds_log.replayed), dashboard (mds_log.ev), Prometheus mixin (ceph_mds_log_evadd/ev/seg).

features.name: Write IO hint selection
features.description: Journal writes carry FADVISE_DONTNEED unless the MDSMap shows a standby-replay follower for the rank; reads always use FADVISE_DONTNEED.

features.name: Writes continue when pools are full
features.description: The MDS objecter does not honour pool-full flags and tags ops CEPH_OSD_FLAG_FULL_FORCE, so journaling (and thus deletes) can proceed on a full cluster.

features.name: Offline journal reset
features.description: cephfs-journal-tool journal reset: soft (new start after old end, header rewrite, EResetJournal) or hard (--force: new pointer, fresh journal, EResetJournal). EResetJournal replay wipes sessions, resets inotable and claims root/mydir subtrees.
features.notes: JournalTool refuses with -EPERM only when the selected rank is up:active in the MDSMap (src/tools/cephfs/JournalTool.cc:148); ranks in replay/clientreplay/stopping pass the check. A hard reset leaves objects of the previous journal inode in place.

features.name: Offline journal inspection, export/import, header edit, event splice
features.description: cephfs-journal-tool scans pointer/header/objects, finds corrupt ranges by sentinel search, exports/imports raw journals, edits header fields, splices events with ENoOp padding, recovers dentries.

features.name: Runtime configuration of mds_log options
features.description: MDLog::handle_conf_change updates cached option values; only keys in MDSRankDispatcher::get_tracked_keys are delivered (mds_log_warn_factor and mds_log_minor_segments_per_major_segment are not).

features.name: Journal pause (mds_log_pause)
features.description: Dev option: the submit thread stops dequeuing events while set; kick_submitter resumes it.

features.name: Expiry kill points
features.description: mds_kill_journal_expire_at 1..5 asserts at defined points of try_to_expire for crash testing.

features.name: Large event detection
features.description: Encoded events >= mds_log_event_large_threshold (512 KiB) increment evlrg.

features.name: Debug subtree maps (mds_debug_subtrees)
features.description: Journals an ESubtreeMap retyped EVENT_SUBTREEMAP_TEST whenever the current segment has more than one event; these still start major segments.

features.name: Op tracker journal events
features.description: Requests record 'submit entry: <fn>' at submission and 'journal_committed: ' when the log completion runs (visible in dump_ops_in_flight/historic ops).

features.name: Read-only mode stops trimming
features.description: When the cache is read-only (e.g. mds_action_on_write_error=1 after a write error), trim() and _maybe_expired return immediately; the journal grows until MDS_TRIM.

features.name: Journal thread shutdown
features.description: MDLog::shutdown drops mds_lock only to signal the submit thread, joins it with mds_lock held (that thread never takes mds_lock), joins the trim thread with mds_lock dropped, shuts down the Journaler (failing waiters with EAGAIN, recovery waiters with ESHUTDOWN) and joins replay/recovery threads with mds_lock dropped.

features.name: Journaler write buffer throttle
features.description: append_entry blocks when buffered unflushed data would exceed UINT_MAX - UINT_MAX>>3 bytes.

features.name: Journaler read prefetch
features.description: Readers prefetch up to journaler_prefetch_periods periods ahead with per-object reads and assimilate contiguous data; entries larger than the window extend it temporarily.

features.name: Journal reformat (legacy-format rewrite) hazards
features.description: _reformat_journal saves JournalPointer.back before writing the new header (a crash there leaves a headerless back journal and every later start goes damaged), waits on Journaler::flush(ctx) which can complete before the tail is durable, and installs no write-error handler on the new Journaler until after the pointer swap (a write error aborts). Legacy-format path only.
features.notes: Only reachable for journals older than mds_journal_format (pre-RESILIENT).

serialization_points.name: MDLog::submit_entry (mds_lock + submit_mutex)
serialization_points.shared_state: event_seq, current segment, pending_events, segment counters
serialization_points.why_serialized: Assigns the per-rank total order and segment membership; callers hold mds_lock anyway.
serialization_points.notes: Only events touching the same objects or the same rank-global tables need relative order.

serialization_points.name: Single mds-log-submit thread
serialization_points.shared_state: Encoding and Journaler append of every event of the rank
serialization_points.why_serialized: One consumer drains pending_events in seq order so the byte stream equals submission order.
serialization_points.notes: Encoding is independent per event; only the append order matters.

serialization_points.name: Journaler single byte stream (Journaler::lock)
serialization_points.shared_state: write_pos, write_buf, flush_pos, pending_safe, safe_pos, waitfor_safe
serialization_points.why_serialized: One log has one append position and one durable prefix.
serialization_points.notes: Inherent per stream; independent per-shard streams would remove the cross-shard conflict.

serialization_points.name: Conservative safe_pos with overlapping flushes
serialization_points.why_serialized: safe_pos only advances to the boundary recorded at issue of the oldest flush pending at completion time (fix d17790f299c).
serialization_points.notes: Adds one flush of latency under continuous load.

serialization_points.name: Completion delivery on mds-rank-fin under mds_lock
serialization_points.shared_state: All cache state touched by log completions (apply of projected state, replies, lock release)
serialization_points.why_serialized: Journaler callbacks are wrapped in C_OnFinisher on the single finisher; each completion takes mds_lock; offset order is preserved.
serialization_points.notes: Completions for unrelated objects could run in parallel.

serialization_points.name: Whole-log flush and wait_for_safe
serialization_points.why_serialized: Flush and barrier semantics are defined over the single stream.
serialization_points.notes: A request needing durability flushes everyone's buffered events.

serialization_points.name: Major segment creation inside submit_mutex
serialization_points.shared_state: Rank subtree map (walk of all subtrees, bounds and spanning tree)
serialization_points.why_serialized: ESubtreeMap must describe the whole rank's authority as replay starting point.
serialization_points.notes: Per-shard checkpoints would only describe one shard.

serialization_points.name: Trim pass under mds_lock (mds-log-trim)
serialization_points.shared_state: Cache dirty lists, dirfrag commit initiation, table saves, OFT commit
serialization_points.why_serialized: Expiry walks shared cache objects; done under the global lock for the whole pass.

serialization_points.name: Trimming in whole major-segment groups
serialization_points.why_serialized: Replay must begin at a major boundary.
serialization_points.notes: Needs some replay starting point; granularity could be per shard.

serialization_points.name: Expiry coupled to rank-global tables
serialization_points.why_serialized: Tables are versioned by the single journal and saved whole.
serialization_points.notes: Sharding tables (ino ranges, per-shard session state) would localize it.

serialization_points.name: OpenFileTable commit gating expiry
serialization_points.why_serialized: Open-file state must cover a segment before it is trimmed.

serialization_points.name: Prezero window, single trim purge, header writes
serialization_points.why_serialized: Flushes stall until objects ahead are removed; one purge at a time; header ordering checks.

serialization_points.name: Single-threaded replay with per-event mds_lock
serialization_points.why_serialized: Events are applied strictly in journal order.
serialization_points.notes: Only events on the same objects/subtrees depend on each other.

serialization_points.name: Client replay one request at a time
serialization_points.why_serialized: During up:clientreplay the next replayed request is queued only after the previous one has been submitted to the journal (MDSRank::queue_one_replay).
serialization_points.notes: Only conflicting replayed requests need ordering; relevant to multi-tenant recovery time.

serialization_points.name: Standby-replay follower passes
serialization_points.why_serialized: One pass at a time over the active's single stream, 1 s apart.

serialization_points.name: Fencing before replay
serialization_points.why_serialized: The previous writer must be blocklisted before the new holder reads/writes.
serialization_points.notes: Needed for any single-writer log; per shard if shards migrate independently.

serialization_points.name: Filer writes issued under Journaler::lock (and mds_lock from MDLog::flush)
serialization_points.shared_state: Journaler positions while Objecter ops are prepared and sent
serialization_points.why_serialized: _do_flush calls Filer::write/zero with Journaler::lock held, and MDLog::flush() reaches it on the caller's thread while mds_lock is held; the Objecter op budget is not blocking in the MDS (keep_balanced_budget unset), so the cost is Objecter lock time, not throttling.
serialization_points.notes: objecter_inflight_ops/objecter_inflight_op_bytes are accounted but not enforced for the MDS Objecter (src/osdc/Objecter.h:2693, MDSRank.cc:483).

serialization_points.name: Stray directory rotation per segment
serialization_points.why_serialized: Couples stray placement to journal activity.

serialization_points.name: Log capping on stop
serialization_points.why_serialized: A stopping rank must reduce its journal to a single major boundary.

external_contract.item: Safe reply only after journal commit
external_contract.detail: For journaled operations the safe MClientReply is sent from the log completion after the event is durable; the kclient keeps requests with only an unsafe reply on s_unsafe and waits on r_safe_completion for fsync/syncfs.

external_contract.item: Unsafe requests replayed after MDS failover
external_contract.detail: When the MDS reaches reconnect the kclient re-sends unsafe requests (and old unanswered ones); the recovering MDS must recognise requests whose events are already in the journal.

Session op 12 with no reply; sent on fsync of an inode with unsafe requests (to all involved MDSes and the auth MDS), syncfs, pre-umount and client reset; only if the MDS connection has SERVER_LUMINOUS.

kclient comment: without an explicit flush 'in the worst case we must wait at most 5 seconds' for the MDS to flush periodically (mds_tick_interval); the C++ MDS skips that tick flush while its beacon is laggy.

external_contract.item: fsync wait on the safe reply (no timeout by default)
external_contract.detail: fsync waits with wait_for_completion_timeout(r_timeout) and returns -EIO on timeout, but r_timeout is 0 (= MAX_SCHEDULE_TIMEOUT) for ordinary requests; only the mount-time root request sets it from mount_timeout, so in practice fsync blocks until the safe reply.
FLUSH_ACK for dirty caps is sent from Locker::file_update_finish, the completion of the EUpdate; fsync waits for it via caps_are_flushed.

libcephfs sends CEPH_SESSION_REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG to the ranks of the inode's unsafe ops plus its auth-cap MDS (fsync, nonblocking fsync) or to every session while requests are outstanding (_sync_fs, unmount), then waits for safe replies.
Ganesha's synchronous metadata/COMMIT paths go through libcephfs fsync/sync, so their latency equals journal commit latency plus the flush trigger.
ceph-fuse uses the libcephfs Client and therefore the same FLUSH_MDLOG and safe-reply behaviour.

Unhandled journal write errors, corrupt or missing journal objects/pointer mark the rank damaged via beacon want_state STATE_DAMAGED (down:damaged, send_and_wait mds_mon_shutdown_timeout), then respawn; cleared by 'ceph mds repaired'.
Beacon health MDS_HEALTH_TRIM ('MDS_TRIM', HEALTH_WARN, 'Behind on trimming (N/M)', metadata num_segments/max_segments) when segments > max_segments*warn_factor.
'ceph mds fail' and 'ceph fs fail' return EPERM without --yes-i-really-mean-it while an affected MDS reports MDS_TRIM (or cache oversized).
In up:replay for more than 30 s the beacon reports percent complete, elapsed and estimated remaining time.
Journal completion contexts older than osd_op_complaint_time count as slow metadata IOs.
The new holder waits for OSD map epoch >= mdsmap last_failure_osd_epoch (previous holder blocklisted) before reading the journal; standby-replay takeover does the same before its final pass.

external_contract.item: Rank states driven by the journal
external_contract.detail: up:creating (create + first ESubtreeMap safe), up:starting (append, ESubtreeMap safe), up:replay (replay done), up:standby-replay (tailing), up:stopping -> down:stopped (journal trimmed and capped with ELid).
While following a rank, the messenger name is mds.<gid> rather than mds.<rank>.

mds_log.{evadd,ev,seg,replayed} (prio interesting) and useful-level counters are sent to the mgr; status module uses mds_log.replayed rate for standby-replay; dashboard uses mds_log.ev (and the nonexistent mds_log.replay); Prometheus mixin uses ceph_mds_log_evadd/ev/seg.
asok/tell 'flush journal' returns JSON {message, return_code}; -EROFS on read-only; no-op when not active.
'cache drop' output contains a flush_journal section {return_code, message}.
status in replay/standby-replay includes replay_status {journal_read_pos, journal_write_pos, journal_expire_pos, num_events, num_segments}.

Pointer <0x400+rank hex>.00000000; journal <0x200+rank hex>.<objno %08llx> with header in object 0 and data from object 1; alternate <0x300+rank hex>.* during reformat; metadata pool, default namespace.

Sequential object writes (commit acks), write_full header and pointer, stat probes with RWORDERED, read with FADVISE_DONTNEED, remove/zero ahead (prezero) and remove behind (trim); write hint DONTNEED unless a follower exists; all ops FULL_FORCE.
Prezero, trim and probe treat ENOENT as success / size 0; other errors are journal write errors.

inspect/export/import/reset/header/event commands parse the pointer, header (magic, positions, legacy layout, stream_format), RESILIENT framing and LogEvent encodings directly; a different on-disk format makes them inapplicable.
first-damage.py instructs 'ceph tell mds.<fs_name>:0 flush journal' before offline scanning; disaster-recovery docs rely on journal reset/recover_dentries.
The tool reads the FSMap and refuses (-EPERM) only if the selected rank is up:active; it relies on operators failing the fs first (first-damage.py runbook) for other states.

rust_implications.implication: The C++ design has exactly one journal per rank, totally ordered; per-subvolume shards need their own journal streams, each with its own replay starting point (checkpoint record equivalent to ESubtreeMap/ELid describing only that shard's authority and state) and trimming at checkpoint granularity.

Clients only require that a safe reply/cap flush ack/session ack implies durability and that unsafe replies may later be replayed; the order of safe replies across unrelated inodes is not observed. A shard journal can commit and complete independently of other shards.

C++ relies on callers, the 5 s tick and client FLUSH_MDLOG to flush; kclient/libcephfs send CEPH_SESSION_REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG (no reply) and assume a periodic flush within ~5 s. A Rust journal can do proactive group commit (flush on idle or after a short delay), but must still accept FLUSH_MDLOG and advertise SERVER_LUMINOUS so clients send it.

C++ events carry full object state so the newest segment that dirtied an object owns its writeback and older segments trim without it. Keeping this property (or per-object LSNs) avoids cross-segment dependencies in a sharded journal.

A segment can only be trimmed after dirfrags, backtraces, inode table, session map, snap/table state and open-file state it depends on are persisted. With autonomous shards, rank-global tables (InoTable, SessionMap completed_requests/prealloc_inos, OpenFileTable, SnapServer) must be sharded or versioned per shard, otherwise every shard's trim depends on global table saves.

Clients resend unsafe requests on reconnect; the C++ MDS finds already-journaled requests via client request ids recorded in events/session state. Each shard journal must record client reqids (and completed-request trimming state) so multi-tenant replay can answer replays correctly.

Single-writer guarantee comes from mon rank assignment + OSD blocklisting + waiting for last_failure_osd_epoch before reading the journal. Any design where shards move between daemons needs the same blocklist/epoch barrier per handover.

RESILIENT framing has a sentinel and start_ptr but no checksum, and torn tails are detected only by length; a new format should add CRCs and sequence numbers so recovery need not rely on probing object sizes and prezeroing.

C++ removes objects ahead of the write position and probes object sizes on recovery; a self-describing record format (seq + CRC) can find the end by reading forward and avoid the extra remove ops per object.

C++ funnels every journal completion through one finisher thread and mds_lock in offset order; per-shard completion queues on a worker pool would remove this global serialization while preserving per-object order.

rust_implications.topic: Trim work under the big lock
rust_implications.implication: The trim pass (dir commits, table saves, backtrace batching) runs under mds_lock for the whole pass; in Rust expiry should be per shard, asynchronous, and rate-limited per shard (useful for per-subvolume QoS/SLA).

Journaler's conservative safe_pos (lag of one overlapping flush) and the lack of time-based flush add latency for synchronous NFS workloads; a Rust journal can track per-write commit ranges precisely.

The mon expects MDS_TRIM (gates 'mds fail'/'fs fail'), MDS_ESTIMATED_REPLAY_TIME and MDS_SLOW_METADATA_IO in beacons, and up:damaged on journal corruption/write errors. A sharded journal must aggregate shard state into these rank-level health metrics.

Keep mds_log.evadd, mds_log.ev, mds_log.seg, mds_log.replayed (and ideally the other mds_log.* names) so ceph fs status, the dashboard and Prometheus dashboards keep working; per-shard counters can be added as labelled counters.

If allow_standby_replay is set the mon assigns up:standby-replay daemons that must tail the rank's journal read-only and be promotable through up:replay; with multiple shard journals the follower must tail all of them (or the fs flag must be documented as unsupported).

Reducing max_mds or upgrades require a stopping rank to reach down:stopped; C++ does this by exporting subtrees, closing sessions, trimming and capping the journal (ELid). The Rust MDS must provide an equivalent drain-and-cap of all its shard journals.
C++ journal writes use FULL_FORCE so deletes can still be journaled when pools are full; a Rust MDS needs the same objecter flag behaviour to avoid deadlock on full clusters.

cephfs-journal-tool, first-damage.py and disaster-recovery runbooks only understand the C++ journal format; the Rust MDS should ship equivalent offline inspect/reset tooling and should refuse to start (not misparse) when it finds C++ journal objects (magic 'ceph fs volume v011' in <0x200+rank>.00000000).

Because the Rust on-disk format is free but lives in the same metadata pool namespace, avoid reusing the 0x200/0x300/0x400/0x500 + rank object names with different contents, or detect and reject pools initialized by the C++ MDS.

C++ treats every journal write error as rank damage (independent of mds_action_on_write_error) and respawns on blocklist/timeout; the Rust MDS should define per-shard failure isolation (quarantine one shard) while keeping the mon-visible damaged semantics for the rank where required.

C++ standby_trim_segments can run on the replay thread without mds_lock while it marks objects clean and trims the cache; a Rust follower should serialize segment trimming with all other cache access by construction (same task/owner).

Journaler::flush(ctx) in C++ can report completion before earlier writes are durable when nothing is buffered; a Rust journal API should make every flush/barrier completion mean 'everything before this point is durable'.
